Changelog

forestBalance 0.1.1

New features

  • forest_balance() and kernel_balance() gain estimand = c("ATE", "ATT", "ATC").

  • Optional ridge penalty lambda (default 0) in all solver paths.

  • kernel.response = c("joint", "treatment", "outcome") selects the responses used to grow the kernel forest.

  • crossfit.balance = c("fold", "full") chooses whether cross-fitted weights are solved on the evaluation fold or on the full sample with the held-out forest.

  • New maxiter argument for the conjugate gradient solver. Fits now return leaf counts, solver iteration counts, and diagnostics for every linear solve (residuals, arm totals, and projected KKT residuals).

Changes in behavior

  • The default ridge penalty is now lambda = 0.1 in forest_balance() and kernel_balance(). Without a ridge, the kernel block of an arm is singular when units share leaves in nearly every tree (for example, with a binary outcome and many covariates), and the balancing weights are then not determined.

  • A numerically singular kernel block now raises an informative error instead of returning arbitrary weights or failing with a generic message, and an ill-conditioned block (condition number above about 10^6) gives a warning that the weights can be extreme. Because kernel entries lie in [0, 1], the condition number of an arm block of size n_a is at most 1 + n_a / lambda, so with the default ridge the warning requires an arm of more than about 100,000 units.

  • The target linear solve now uses the right-hand side n_a^2 b_a directly instead of rescaling its solution by n_a^2, so solver error is no longer amplified by the squared arm size. A small positive lambda with the iterative solvers at large n no longer fails the final accuracy check. Weights are mathematically unchanged.

  • The block Jacobi solver (solver = "bj") now stops on the same absolute residual criterion as the conjugate gradient solver. Its relative criterion left errors that grew with the target right-hand side and failed the final accuracy check under a positive lambda at large n.

  • Failed linear solves or failed weight accuracy checks now raise an error carrying the diagnostics; version 0.1.0 returned weights without these checks. Cross-fitted estimates no longer drop failed folds when averaging.

Compatibility

  • src/cg_solve.cpp uses Map<SparseMatrix> for compatibility with Eigen 5 (thanks to Dirk Eddelbuettel, #1).

forestBalance 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-04-07

Initial release.

Features

  • forest_balance(): High-level ATE estimation with forest kernel energy balancing. Supports K-fold cross-fitting (default) and adaptive min.node.size selection.

  • Adaptive min.node.size heuristic: max(20, min(floor(n/200) + p, floor(n/50))). Scales leaf size with sample size and dimension to balance bias and variance.

  • Two linear solvers with automatic selection:

    • Direct: sparse Cholesky on treated/control sub-blocks. Used for moderate sample sizes.
    • Conjugate gradient (CG): matrix-free solver using the factored kernel representation. Avoids forming the full kernel matrix for large n.

  • Rcpp-accelerated leaf node extraction from GRF forests (C++ tree traversal).

  • Sparse kernel construction via single tcrossprod on the leaf indicator matrix.

  • compute_balance(): Covariate balance diagnostics (SMD, ESS, energy distance) with support for nonlinear transformations.

  • simulate_data(): Synthetic data generation with nonlinear confounding for demonstrations and testing.
